title: Horoscopes and modern idolatry
intro: Only Allah knows the unseen – why a Muslim does not follow horoscopes, fortune-tellers or superstitions.

learn.title: 📜 Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Whoever goes to a fortune-teller and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad (SAW).” (Tirmidhi)
Writing horoscopes, drawing them and believing what a horoscope says all fall under this hadith.
A person who writes horoscopes and “predicts” the future directly denies the meaning of the ayah in which Allah tells us that no one except Him knows the unseen (ghayb).

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Say: no one in the heavens or on the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not even know when they will be raised back to life. <small>(Qur’an, An-Naml 27:65, meaning)</small>

Many people say they read horoscopes just for fun, doubting them or not believing them. Even worse and more dangerous is to truly trust a horoscope. Believing someone who claims to know the future is an act of kufr (disbelief).
If we watch people who follow horoscopes, we see that however much they say they don’t believe them, they are happy when they read something they like – and scared when they read something bad.
The word idolatry comes from two Greek words: eidolon, which means “image” or “idol”, and latreia, which means “worship”. So idolatry means worshipping idols.

People say – knowingly or not – that they “worship” food, TV shows, films, actors or players, and this is presented as something normal, as a kind of love. A Muslim must always remember to worship, in words and in deeds, only Allah (SWT). Worshipping someone or something other than Allah can take a person out of Islam.
Other forms of idolatry today are called superstitions, for example:

items.label: A black cat crossing your path “brings bad luck”
Knocking on wood “so nothing bad happens”

learn.html: These are only excuses of people who do not have complete faith in Allah (SWT). A believer trusts Allah, not signs, stars or luck.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Only Allah knows the unseen and the future. Our destiny was decreed and written before we were born – not by the stars and not by a horoscope.

items.text: Studying hard and then relying on Allah

practice.title: Who knows the future?
practice.prompt: Tap every sentence that is true, then tap Check.

options.text: Believing a fortune-teller is a serious sin – the hadith calls it disbelief
Our destiny was written before we were born
Horoscopes are fine if you only read them for fun
options.why: The book warns that even “for fun” people end up happy or scared by what they read – a Muslim stays away from them.

options.text: The stars decide whether you will have a good day
options.why: Allah decides everything – the stars are His creation, not a sign of our luck.

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) say about believing a fortune-teller?
options: That person has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad (SAW)

questions.q: Which surah says that no one but Allah knows the unseen (27:65)?
Where does the word “idolatry” come from?
options: Two Greek words: eidolon (image) and latreia (worship)

questions.q: Which of these is a superstition?
options: A broken mirror brings bad luck

questions.q: Why is it a problem to say we “worship” a player or a TV show?
options: A Muslim worships only Allah, in words and deeds

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: ❓ What did the Prophet (SAW) say about fortune-telling? What do people who read and believe horoscopes deny?
❓ What is idolatry? Which modern forms of idolatry exist today?

🔢 Task 1: About 8 billion people live in the world, and horoscopes divide them into only 12 signs – so hundreds of millions of people would have the “same fate” every day. Even if there were 100,000 signs, thousands of people would still share one fate at the same moment. Is that possible?

✍️ Task 2: Draw a word map with “Destiny” in the middle. Around it, write things about a person’s life that Allah decreed and wrote before the person was born (for example: when we are born, our provision, our lifespan).
